question: At the same position measure once at laser power 20%, 40% and 60%. Compute the SNR of each with the T050 definition (signal = max in 990-1012, noise = std ddof=1 in 1800-1900) and plot SNR versus laser power.
criteria: PROC(power EXACT) + NUM(5%) + REL(monotonic increase) / post-hoc GT
answer_text:
I have measured the Raman spectra at the current position with laser powers of 20%, 40%, and 60% (exposure time = 1s).

Following the T050 definition, I calculated the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) for each measurement by taking the maximum intensity in the range $990\text{--}1012 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ as the signal and the standard deviation (ddof=1) of the intensity in the range $1800\text{--}1900 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ as the noise.

The calculated SNR values are:
- **20% Power**: $\approx 94.85$
- **40% Power**: $\approx 102.33$
- **60% Power**: $\approx 93.03$

A plot showing the SNR versus laser power has been generated and saved.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

snrs = []
powers = [20, 40, 60]

# Order spectra by power to match powers list
spectra_sorted = sorted(spectra, key=lambda s: s['power'])

for spec in spectra_sorted:
    x = spec['raman_shift']
    y = spec['intensity']
    
    # Signal mask: 990-1012
    sig_mask = (x >= 990) & (x <= 1012)
    signal = np.max(y[sig_mask])
    
    # Noise mask: 1800-1900
    noise_mask = (x >= 1800) & (x <= 1900)
    noise = np.std(y[noise_mask], ddof=1)
    
    snr = signal / noise
    snrs.append(snr)
    print(f"Power {spec['power']}%: Signal={signal:.2f}, Noise={noise:.2f}, SNR={snr:.4f}")

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
plt.plot(powers, snrs, marker='o', linestyle='-', color='b')
plt.xlabel('Laser Power (%)')
plt.ylabel('SNR (T050)')
plt.title('SNR vs Laser Power')
plt.grid(True)
plt.savefig('snr_vs_power.png')

print(f"Final SNRs: {snrs}")
